findings.title: Informational rate-limit events are routed two different ways
findings.description:
Task 6 says that for an informational event, `_skip_unparseable` should "log at DEBUG and continue the loop without yielding it to the caller" and, in the same bullet, "let it flow to translation as normal." `_skip_unparseable` reaches translation only by yielding, so both cannot hold. Task 7 (line 70) sends informational events to `translate_sdk_message` in `dispatch`.

The slice design has the same conflict. D4 (lines 264–266) says informational events "must not reach translation." D6 and the Task 4 rationale say they must reach translation to become observable. The data-flow block (lines 326–330) states both.

If Task 6 is followed, Task 4's branch is unreachable in query and client mode, and the three paths behave differently. I recommend translating informational events in all three paths, as D6 and Task 7 say. Rewrite Task 6's bullet and correct D4 to match. This choice determines the next finding.

findings.title: Translated notices leak through four consumers that Task 8 does not cover
findings.description:
Once Task 4 emits a `system` message with `sdk_type: rate_limit_event`, every agent-path consumer receives it. Only `sdk_session.dispatch` excludes it (Task 8). These sites append it to their output:

- `src/squadron/review/review_client.py:263-265` excludes `(SDK_RESULT_TYPE, "tool_use", "tool_result")`, then appends. This is the `sq review` path. Task 14 and design walkthrough step 3 require that a notice "must not appear in the artifact's prose," and this file builds the text the verdict is parsed from.
- `src/squadron/pipeline/summary_oneshot.py:139-141` uses the same tuple, then appends.
- `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py:557-559` excludes only `SDK_RESULT_TYPE` (tool events are handled earlier), then appends.
- `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:165-167` excludes only `SDK_RESULT_TYPE`, then appends.

Task 8 asks the implementer to grep for `SDK_RESULT_TYPE` and decide, but its success criterion covers only `dispatch`. Task 4 also does not say what `content` the message carries.

Fix:
- Define one shared set of non-prose `sdk_type` values next to `SDK_RESULT_TYPE` (`src/squadron/core/models.py:111-112`), and use it at all five sites. This follows the "define comparison values once" rule.
- Name the sites in Task 8.
- Put Task 8 in the same commit as Task 4. Currently Task 4 (line 46) commits before Task 8 (line 77), which leaves a window where notices reach prose.

findings.title: Two intermediate commits are red
findings.description:
Task 6 removes the `is_rate_limit_event` special case in `_skip_unparseable`. `test_a_rejected_rate_limit_event_reaches_the_backoff` (line 648) raises a `MessageParseError` carrying a `rejected` payload, so it now logs and skips, and the test fails. Task 10 fixes it later.

Task 9 deletes `install_rate_limit_parser_shim`. The four shim tests import it inside their bodies (`test_agent.py:701, 720, 743, 758`), and Task 10 deletes them later.

A file without `**Commit**:` markers commits at the end of each top-level task, so the history contains red commits. Add markers at green points (after Task 5, after Task 11, after Task 13), or merge Tasks 6–11 into one commit.

findings.title: Task 3's fixture is the fabrication that Task 10 forbids
findings.description:
Task 3 adds a test asserting `_is_throttle(ClaudeSDKError("rate_limit_event: slow down"))` in `test_agent.py`, which it names first. Task 10's success check (line 99) requires zero `ClaudeSDKError("rate_limit_event` constructions in that file. Criterion 9 calls that construction a dead-path fabrication.

Use a genuine-429 text that does not contain `rate_limit_event` (for example, `"API Error: 429 rate_limit exceeded"`) in Task 3 and in the loop test recommended below.

findings.title: Criterion 7 loses its only loop-level test
findings.description:
Criterion 7 requires a plain `ClaudeSDKError` containing `rate_limit` to trigger backoff, not just pass the predicate. Today `test_retries_actually_sleep` (line 526), `test_stats_accumulate_across_retries` (around line 612) and `test_exhausted_rate_limit_raises_a_distinct_error` (around line 639) drive that path. Task 10 rewrites all three onto `RateLimitEvent`. Task 3 unit-tests only `_is_throttle`.

After Task 10, no test drives backoff through the substring path. Keep one loop-level test in Task 10 that raises the 429-text `ClaudeSDKError` on every call and asserts retries and sleeps.

findings.title: Criterion 3 is not assigned per dispatch path, and no task asserts the WARNING
findings.description:
Criterion 3 requires a rejected event to trigger backoff in all three paths, with a WARNING naming the attempt number. Task 10 does not say which mode each rewritten test covers. `_handle_client_mode` (`agent.py:184`) has no assigned rejected-event test. No task asserts the WARNING or the `throttles` increment in the client path.

Name one rejected-yield test each for query mode, client mode (in `TestClientModeErrors`, `test_agent.py:348`) and `dispatch` (Task 11). Each should assert `RateLimitStats.throttles` and the WARNING.

findings.title: An abandoned live stream is not closed before restart
findings.description:
Task 6 raises `RateLimitRejected` from inside `_skip_unparseable` while the SDK stream is still alive, which is the behavior D4 intends. Nothing tells the implementer to close that stream before the outer loop starts a new query or `receive_response()`. D4 says "restarting a healthy stream is safe" without addressing cleanup.

The failure-mode rule in `.claude/rules/review-code.md` requires each new failure path to be enumerated, including what the stream does when the raise happens. Specify closing the underlying iterator (for example, `aclose()` in a `finally`) on the rejected path, with a test asserting it. Task 7's inline raise in `dispatch` needs the same.

findings.title: The load-test tier is not addressed
findings.description:
The project's Python rules (Testing & Quality, load-test tier) require at least one `tests/load/` test for code on network or concurrency paths, and CI gating for slices that touch them. This slice changes the stream-consumption and retry gates in `agent.py` and `sdk_session.py`.

The breakdown has no load task and no CI task. `tests/load/test_grep_timeout.py` exists. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has ruff and pyright steps at lines 28–30, and nothing in it names `tests/load`.

Either add a load task (for example, a throttled stream that must back off within budget without starving the loop) plus a CI wiring task, or record why the rule does not apply. Whether it applies is a Project Manager call, but the breakdown should not leave it implicit.

findings.title: The slice is split into 16 tasks, more than a "small diff" needs
findings.description:
There are 16 top-level tasks and 15 commit lines across about 10 files. The design rates effort 3/5 and calls the production diff small. Suggested merges:

- Tasks 2+3 and 4+5: each helper or branch lands with its tests.
- Tasks 6–11: one code-and-test change, since they depend on each other (see the red-commit finding).
- Task 12 into Task 13. Task 12 changes nothing. Grep finds no shim reference in `tests/providers/sdk/test_provider.py`, so the design's "requiring the criterion-9 rewrite" heading for that file and `test_audit_cli.py` is inaccurate. Task 12's confirmation belongs in the run in Task 13.
- Task 13's first two pytest runs are subsets of the full-suite run. Keep one.

Tasks 3 and 5 add unit tests that no success criterion names. Keep them if wanted, but they count as commits. The result would be about five commits at working points.

findings.title: Task 5 says to create a file that already exists
findings.description: Task 5 says to create `tests/providers/sdk/test_translation.py` "if it does not exist." The file exists and has `translate_sdk_message` tests through line 287. Name the file and say to add the test to it.

findings.title: Criterion 2's `tests/` clause has no check
findings.description: Criterion 2 and walkthrough step 1 grep `install_rate_limit_parser_shim` in both `src` and `tests`. Task 9's success check greps only `src`. Task 10 deletes the four shim tests (lines 701, 720, 743, 758), but no task checks `tests/` for the symbol. Add the `tests/` grep to Task 10's success check.
